attachments.origin_landmark: petrous temporal bone and the cartilage of the pharyngotympanic tube
attachments.insertion_landmark: upper surface of the palatine aponeurosis

actions: elevates the soft palate to seal the nasopharynx during swallowing and speech

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The principal elevator of the palate, and so the muscle of velopharyngeal closure. Its failure produces hypernasal speech and nasal regurgitation.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound-guided technique -- described only as part of a combined paratubal-muscle injection (with tensor veli palatini and salpingopharyngeus) for patulous eustachian tube/autophonia, on the hypothesis that abnormal activity of these three muscles keeps the tube abnormally patent. The source does not give levator veli palatini its own separate landmark, dose, or approach distinct from the group injection.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Diagnosis and treatment response for the target condition (autophonia from a patulous eustachian tube) are confirmed with posterior rhinoscopy/nasopharyngoscopy and impedance audiometry/tympanometry rather than by EMG of this specific muscle.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Evidence is thin and indirect: levator veli palatini is named as one of three co-injected paratubal muscles in a single case report of BoNT for autophonia, with symptom relief lasting about 9 months, rather than being independently studied or dosed. No dedicated levator-veli-palatini-specific technique was found; this is reported as a group-injection component, not a worked-out muscle-specific approach.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Olthoff A, Laskawi R, Kruse E, 'Successful treatment of autophonia with botulinum toxin: case report', Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol 116(8):594-598 (2007), doi:10.1177/000348940711600807 -- retrieved via PubMed.
